tasks.title: CLI query targets accept paths relative to the working directory

query.text:
`code-atlas query similar --snippet` lets me pass a path relative to where I run the command: from inside `acme-billing/src` I can write `--snippet money.rs:1-15` and it works. Every other query that takes a target only understands paths relative to a repository root. From `acme-api/src/users`, `code-atlas query symbol users.service.ts:18` answers "not found", and so do `query callers ./users.service.ts:18` and an absolute path to the same file.

Please make file targets on the command line resolve against the current working directory (relative and absolute paths) the same way the snippet option already does, for every `code-atlas query` subcommand that takes a target: `symbol`, `callers`, `callees`, `dependents`, `dependencies`, `impact` (each of its targets), `tests-for`, `similar <target>`, `explain` and `read`. Targets that are not a file under one of the project's repositories must keep working exactly as today: repo-relative paths such as `src/users/users.service.ts:18` run from another repository, `repo:path[:line]`, symbol names, entity keys and endpoints like `GET /users/{id}`. The MCP server is not affected; its targets stay repo-relative.

tasks.title: Refactor: one shared place for detector import checks

query.text:
Tech debt in atlas-detect: several framework detectors decide whether they apply to a file by pattern-matching `atlas_core::ImportFact` variants by hand (TS `import` vs `require()` specifiers, Rust `use` roots, plus a fallback on path-qualified references), and the same logic exists a second time for detectors that already work on a parsed file. Every new detector copies one of these snippets and they have started to drift.

Extract one shared abstraction inside atlas-detect for "which modules/crates does this file import" and route every existing check through it. After the change, no file under `crates/atlas-detect/src/detectors/` may mention `ImportFact` any more.

This is a pure refactor: no detector may start or stop applying to any file, and detection output must stay byte-identical. The existing checks are not all equally permissive (for example in how they treat `require()` or `extern crate`); keep each one exactly as it is today and do not "fix" those differences in this change. Keep the existing tests green.

tasks.title: Expose the dependents/dependencies traversals as MCP tools

query.text:
Agents connected through the MCP server cannot ask "what uses this?" or "what does this use?".

The CLI already answers both with `code-atlas query dependents <target>` and `code-atlas query dependencies <target>`, which follow imports, type usage, references, inheritance and so on. The MCP server only offers `atlas_callers` / `atlas_callees`, which follow calls only, so an agent asking which modules depend on a class gets nothing useful.

Please add two MCP tools, `atlas_dependents` and `atlas_dependencies`, that answer the same questions as those CLI commands. They should be indistinguishable from the existing call-traversal tools in everything an agent relies on: the same argument names, defaults and validation (`target` required, optional `depth` and `format`), the same text and JSON output, the same not-found / ambiguous handling, read-only annotations, and an agent-facing description that, like the other relation tools, warns that [heuristic]/[inferred] relations must be verified. Keep the server's existing tests passing.

Per-repository file size limit.

A project has a single `max_file_bytes` setting (`[project.settings]` in `projects.toml`) that applies to every repo in the project. In mixed projects that is too blunt: one of our repos has large hand-maintained TypeScript files that we want indexed, another vendors huge files we never want to parse, and raising or lowering the project-wide value fixes one repo while breaking the other.

Please let each `[[project.repo]]` entry in `projects.toml` optionally set its own `max_file_bytes`. When a repo sets it, that value replaces the project setting for that repo, whether it is larger or smaller; repos that don't set it keep using the project setting. The limit must be honoured consistently, for the first full index as well as for later freshness scans and incremental updates. Registries written by the current version must keep loading, and saving the registry must not add the key to repos that don't use it. No CLI flag is needed for now. Keep the whole workspace (including every test target) compiling and the existing tests passing.

tasks.title: Default SameSite=Lax for cookies created by the cookie helper

query.text:
Cookies created through `hono/cookie` (`setCookie`, `setSignedCookie`, `generateCookie`, `generateSignedCookie`, `deleteCookie`) omit the `SameSite` attribute unless the caller passes `sameSite`. Browsers disagree on what a missing attribute means, and security scanners flag every `Set-Cookie` header we emit.

Please make `SameSite=Lax` the default when no `sameSite` option is given:

- it applies to plain, signed, `__Secure-` and `__Host-` prefixed cookies, and to the cookie that `deleteCookie` sends;
- an explicit `sameSite` option always wins;
- the low-level `serialize()` / `serializeSigned()` in `hono/utils/cookie` keep their current output (no implicit default), because other code builds raw cookies with them.

This changes the exact `Set-Cookie` strings Hono produces, so existing tests that assert on them will need updating. CI runs the core test suite and the tests of every adapter package in the workspace (`pnpm test:adapters`, which needs a fresh `vp pack` build of hono first); both must stay green.

Environment note: dependencies are already installed. The global `pnpm` shim on this machine cannot run the pinned pnpm 12.6.0, so use `npx pnpm@12.6.0 ...` or the binaries in `./node_modules/.bin` (for example `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project main <files>`).

tasks.title: Lambda adapters base64-encode textual responses such as text/markdown and text/event-stream

query.text:
Responses with `Content-Type: text/markdown`, `text/event-stream`, `text/calendar` or `application/javascript` come back base64-encoded from our AWS Lambda deployment (API Gateway REST without binary media types configured shows the base64 text to the client), and Lambda@Edge marks the same responses with `bodyEncoding: 'base64'`. Only a short allowlist of `text/*` subtypes is treated as text today.

Expected: the default binary detection treats every `text/*` media type, plus `application/javascript` and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, as text (case-insensitive, with or without parameters such as `charset`). Everything else keeps today's behaviour: JSON and `+json`/`+xml` types stay text, the Apple installer and Mozilla XUL `+xml` types stay binary, and other types (images, fonts, `application/octet-stream`, ...) stay binary.

We reproduce this with both the built-in `hono/aws-lambda` / `hono/lambda-edge` adapters and the standalone `@hono/aws-lambda` / `@hono/lambda-edge` packages, so please fix it everywhere it applies and cover it with tests. The standalone packages test against a `vp pack` build of hono.

Environment note: dependencies are already installed. The global `pnpm` shim on this machine cannot run the pinned pnpm 12.6.0, so use `npx pnpm@12.6.0 ...` or the binaries in `./node_modules/.bin` (for example `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project main <files>`).

tasks.title: WWW-Authenticate challenges do not escape backslashes in quoted-string parameters

query.text:
We configured `bearerAuth({ token, realm: 'C:\\vault' })` and clients receive `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="C:\vault"`, which they parse as `C:vault`. A realm that ends with a backslash even produces an unterminated quoted-string. Double quotes in the realm are escaped, but backslashes are not.

On top of that, when the challenge is configured as an object, e.g. `invalidToken: { wwwAuthenticateHeader: { error: 'invalid_token', error_description: 'bad "token"' } }`, the values are not escaped at all and the header is cut short.

Please escape every quoted-string auth-param per RFC 9110 section 5.6.4 (each backslash and each double quote is preceded by a backslash), consistently in every built-in middleware that emits a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, not just bearer auth. Challenges that the user supplies verbatim as a string (directly or returned from a function) must be sent untouched. Existing behaviour for realms without backslashes must not change. Add tests.

Environment note: dependencies are already installed. The global `pnpm` shim on this machine cannot run the pinned pnpm 12.6.0, so use `npx pnpm@12.6.0 ...` or the binaries in `./node_modules/.bin` (for example `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project main <files>`).
